The above forty-one phrases of the *Caturdaśī* [Dhāraṇī] are a divine mantra spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in sixty-two billion Ganges Rivers.
If anyone should invade or destroy this Dharma-preacher, [this mantra shall protect them].
This would constitute an offense against and destruction of all these Buddhas.
This dhāraṇī brings great benefit to all sentient beings.

The second, the Bodhisattva Śūradatta, spoke this dhāraṇī: *Tadyathā:* 1. *jāpare* 2. *mahājāpare* 3. *ukke* 4. *mukke* 5. *ādite* 6. *ātapati* 7. *nartaye* 8. *nartayapate* 9. *icchinne* 10. *nicchinne* 11. *vicchinne* 12. *narticchinne* 13. *nartapate* "World-Honored One, this is the dhāraṇī."
As taught by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges:
if anyone should injure or defame this Dharma-preacher,
they would thereby have injured and defamed those Buddhas.

The Third, King Vaiśravaṇa, spoke: *Tadyathā:* 1. Ā 2. Kī 3. Nakī 4. Nanana-kī 5. Ānanda-thu 6. Nacche 7. Kuṇacche The Fourth, King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, spoke: *Tadyathā:* 1. Ā 2. Gāṇe 3. Gāṇe 4. Gauri 5. Khandhāri 6. Caṇḍāli 7. Mātangi 8. Pukkasi 9. Saṃkule 10. Pharusāle O World-Honored One, this is the dhāraṇī.
This has been spoken by forty-two billion Buddhas.
If anyone should injure or defame this Dharma-preacher,
they would thereby have injured and defamed these Buddhas.
If anyone does not comply with my mantra and disturbs the Dharma Master, their head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Thus spoke the sixth, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. *Tadyathā*: Āḥ.

The Dharani for Circumambulating Stupas to Eradicate Sins: *Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | kharavalaje | sukhavalaje | gavalaje svāhā.* If any person can, with a sincere heart and a single thought, [recite] this mantra:
During seven days, he circumambulated the stupa and practiced walking meditation,
reciting [the mantra] twelve thousand times;
he then beheld the majestic power of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva face to face.

This mantra for extinguishing all karmic obstacles and fulfilling all aspirations, which extinguishes sins through prostration and brings the Buddhas to welcome one at the end of life, is as follows: Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | ūm | hulu hulu | sthiradharaṇi-sambara-tasādani svāhā | This mantra appears in the *Ratnaketu-dhāraṇī Sūtra*.
As spoken by ten billion bodhisattvas:
reciting this mantra once and prostrating before the Buddha once surpasses the merit of prostrating before the Buddha ten quadrillion times.
It is further said that this is a mantra for the Buddhas to come and welcome one at the end of life.
One should recite it one hundred times during each of the two periods of morning and midday.
Many Brahmin monks frequently recite this mantra.

The Mantra for Making Offerings to the Triple Gem: Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ saṃghāya | namo āryavalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | dhuvi | dhuvi | gāye | dhuvipare dhuvipareṇi svāhā || This mantra should be recited at dawn before an image of the Buddha.
With palms joined and a sincere heart, recite this once daily.
This is superior to making offerings of various incenses and flowers to ten trillion buddhas.

The Avalokiteśvara Repentance Dharani: Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | tura tura | asme asme asme mahāmarīci dūṣamariṇi | dūpe dūpe namaḥ namo namaḥ svāhā || Recite this dharani before an image of Avalokiteśvara.
Burn incense, reveal your transgressions, and repent with a sincere heart;
recite this three times, and the sins accumulated since beginningless time shall be extinguished, while your prayers for fulfillment will surely bear fruit.
The Vajra Snake Mantra: *Namo vajrarājabhānaye mahāyakṣiṇīpādāye citre citre svāhā*. If a person is bitten by a snake and afflicted by its venom, [recite this mantra].
If one recites this mantra twenty-one times, the poison will immediately dissipate and vanish.

This is the *Dhyāna-sukha-pratiṣṭhāpana-mantra* (The Mantra for Establishing Peace and Stability in Meditation). *Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | tadyathā | maha-pade | atipade | vipada-vigata-raja-si | mahā-vigata-raja-si | svāhā.* If, when first sitting in meditation, the mind and body have not yet settled and remain uneasy, [one should recite this mantra].
First, having recited this mantra seven times,
one shall sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) and remain undisturbed.

*Oṃ amoghapāśa-dhāraṇīye svāhā | mahā-svāhāye | mahā-karuṇike svāhā | tadyathā | kili kili | kiri kiri | vikiri vikiri | svāhā.* If there is malignant swelling or wind-swelling (*vāta-gulma*), [recite this].
Chanting the mantra over sesame oil, apply it to the affected area.

The Vajra Mantra for Healing Diseases Caused by Malevolent Spirits: *Namo ratnatrayāya*. Namo maheśvarāya vāsavarājāya. Mahāyakṣasenāpataye. Tadyathā: Sarasara. Ciri ciri. Suru suru. Vindhaya vindhaya. Gṛhṇa hūṃ. Jaḥ liṃ. He he vāsavarājānapate. Kuru kuru. Dhama dhama. Namo svastaye. Svāhā. If a person is afflicted by a spirit-disease, [this mantra should be recited].
Recite the mantra seven times over water and hold it in your hand;
facing the patient, strike them with it while shouting the command, and they will immediately recover.

The second mantra, the second mantra: *Namaḥ ratnatrayāya* (1) *namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya* (2) *bodhisattvāya* (3) *mahāsattvāya* (4) *mahākāruṇikāya* (5) *tadyathā* (6) *om* (7) *tuttāre* (8) *tuttāre* (9) *ture svāhā* (10) *hara hara sarvapāpāni me śodhaya śodhaya svāhā* (11) *sarva-buddha-dharma-śrīye svāhā* (12) *svāhā* (13). Recite this mantra one hundred thousand times.
One shall attain freedom from fear of all heterodox paths;
those who wish to harm me shall find they cannot succeed.

[The third mantra: *Tadyathā | namo ratnatrayāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | citte citta-ri | nāmojini harita-muḥ | dūta-muḥ | duḥ | oṃ muḥ viśuddhe svāhā.* Recite this mantra one hundred thousand times.
It purifies all karmic obstructions.

The Fourth Dhāraṇī: Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | Tadyathā | oṃ hūṃ para-saṃjñā | niryātaye | tattat | parasamne parasamne | parasannākaruṇe | sara prasādapanā hūṃ | karuṇā-praśama-ni svāhā || This dhāraṇī removes ill-will.
Reciting this seven times causes one who is angry to become joyful.

The Seven Koṭi Buddhas’ Divine Mantra, the Seven Koṭi Buddhas’ Divine Mantra: *Namo sarvatathāgata-aryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā | jvale sujvale | cundi svāhā.* The Divine Mantra that Follows the Intent of All Tathāgatas, the Divine Mantra that Follows the Intent of All Tathāgatas: *Namo sarvatathāgatāryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā | oṃ kuru kuru kiri svāhā.* If a person can recite each of these two divine mantras once, [the benefits shall be obtained].
It can extinguish the sins committed during ninety million great kalpas.

Regarding the Six-Syllable Dhāraṇī mantra: *Oṃ vākye dhanam ko*. The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī has provided a commentary on this in six thousand verses. The Tripiṭaka Master states: "By reciting this mantra, one extinguishes all sins and gives rise to all virtues."

I take refuge in the Three Jewels. The mantra for taking refuge in the Three Jewels: Namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namo saṃghāya, mahā-ṛṣibhyo ’smad-bhartṛbhyaḥ. Having recited this mantra, one should say: "Homage! (namas).
In whatever place one is born, may one always encounter the Triple Gem.
May one obtain the four types of close attendance, following like a shadow follows a form without being separated for even a moment.
[May one receive] various miscellaneous dhāraṇīs and sūtras.
